problemStatement.formal: theorem sidon_of_sumset_size (A : Set ℕ) (hfin : A.Finite) (h : (sumset A).ncard = A.ncard * (A.ncard + 1) / 2) : IsSidonSet A
problemStatement.plain: Prove the converse of sidon_sumset_size: if a finite set A of natural numbers has |A+A| = |A|(|A|+1)/2, then A is a Sidon set. Combined with the forward direction (already proved in Erdos156Problem.lean), this gives a complete characterization: A is Sidon iff |A+A| = |A|(|A|+1)/2.
whyMatters: Completes a bijective characterization of Sidon sets via sumset cardinality
Demonstrates that maximal sumset growth is equivalent to all-distinct sums
Useful for checking the Sidon property via counting rather than pair enumeration

proven: Forward direction: IsSidonSet A → |A+A| = |A|(|A|+1)/2 (proved in Erdos156Problem.lean)

currentState.focus: Initial creation as follow-up from erdos-156 completion
currentState.nextAction: Prove sidon_of_sumset_size by contrapositive: if A is not Sidon, show |A+A| < |A|(|A|+1)/2

insights: Proof strategy: contrapositive. If A is not Sidon, there exist a≤b, c≤d with a+b=c+d but {a,b}≠{c,d}. Then the sum map (a,b)↦a+b on {(a,b)|a≤b} is not injective, so |A+A| < |{ordered pairs}| = |A|(|A|+1)/2.
The forward direction proof already established injectivity of the sum map on ordered pairs (sidon_sum_injOn). The converse needs: non-injectivity of this map implies not-Sidon.
Key infrastructure already exists: sumset_eq_image, card_upper_tri, sidon_sum_injOn
nextSteps: May need to handle the edge case of the ordered-pair reduction carefully
